speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, did you have any specific trauma to your right hip or groin area during the rear-end collision?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear a "pop" or "snap" sound in your right hip at the moment of impact, and did you find it difficult or impossible to bear weight immediately after the accident?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Pelvis AP and Lateral. REQUEST IMAGES: Right Hip X-Ray series. Did you have a history of previous hip problems or dislocations before this accident?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic_X-ray: No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Patient
text: Alert and active. No head injury, abdominal pain, or chest pain reported. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That diagnosis does not align with the specific signs of a right hip dislocation you described, such as the leg being shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated. Given your age and the mechanism of injury, could you confirm if you are currently unable to move your right leg or if there is significant bruising in the groin area?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Right Hip. REQUEST IMAGES: Right Hip X-Ray series.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Right Hip: Confirms posterior dislocation of the right hip with associated soft tissue edema and no evidence of acute fracture. No signs consistent with acute appendicitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Posterior Dislocation of the Right Hip. The classic presentation of a shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated leg following a high-energy trauma, confirmed by MRI, rules out acute appendicitis. I will proceed with closed reduction and orthopedic stabilization.
